newsitem.title: GERMANY: Sale of Vulkan unit STN Atlas nears end - official.
newsitem.headline: Sale of Vulkan unit STN Atlas nears end - official.

text.p: Bankrupt German shipbuilder Bremer Vulkan AG is close to completing the sale of its STN Atlas Eletronik defence unit, court-appointed administrator Jobst Wellensiek said on Monday.
In answer to a Reuter enquiry, Wellensiek said the sale, which has been said to have been in its final stages since late October, should be completed before the end of this month.

Wellensiek denied reports that Bremer Vulkan's only profit-making unit would be split apart and sold to separate companies. "The goal is to sell the unit as one piece and talks are continuing," Wellensiek told Reuters.

Among the possible buyers are Mannesmann AG, Rheinmetall and British Aerospace, Wellensiek said, adding there was "kernel of truth" in reports that talks with Mannesmann were not progressing statisfactorily.
But a Mannesmann spokesman confirmed the group was still involved in the talks.
Wellensiek also said he still expected to sell the unit for some 600 million marks, within the expected range of 400 to 800 million marks.

Bremer Vulkan collapsed in May after posting huge losses and being accused of having misappropriated hundreds of millions of marks in state aid cleared by the European Union for use in eastern Germany.
Losses of 1.5 billion marks last year wiped out parent Bremer Vulkan's equity capital, but STN posted an operating profit of 32.5 million marks on sales of 1.45 billion marks.
